observations: Photos show a large rectangular solar panel, front (photo 0, 1) with visible mono-type half-cut cells arranged in rows, aluminum frame.
Back of panel (photo 2, 3) shows a white backsheet, a junction box, and two MC4-style connector cables.
A small printed specification label is visible on the back center in photo 3 but the text is too small/blurred to read any wattage, voltage, or model number.
No brand name or model number is legible on the panel itself anywhere in the four photos; 'NETWORK SOLAR VENTURES' is a seller watermark, not a panel brand.
Panel is shown standing in what looks like a storage/shop area with sacks, cables, and other stock in the background; no visible cracks or frame damage in the shots.
Strong glare/reflection across the front cells in photo 0 and 1 obscures parts of the glass surface, limiting inspection for micro-cracks or hotspots.
No multimeter, inverter display, or any performance test is shown in any photo.

claims.claim: Implied dealer in solar equipment ('Network Solar Venture... We deal...')
claims.evidence: No business registration, storefront signage, or third-party proof shown in photos.

claims.claim: Panel is functional / produces rated power (implied by listing as a sellable panel)
claims.evidence: No test shot (multimeter reading, inverter display, or sunlight output test) in any photo.
Glare in photo 0 and 1 obscures parts of the cell surface; no close-up of corners or frame joints to confirm no micro-cracks or dents.

risks.risk: Actual wattage/voltage rating unknown, which is the primary price driver for a solar panel
risks.proof: Clear, well-lit close-up photo of the rear specification label showing model, wattage (Wp), Voc, Isc, Vmp, Imp
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this; wattage range too wide to assume worst case meaningfully

risks.risk: Cell micro-cracks or hotspots not visible due to glare
risks.proof: Photos taken without direct glare, and an electroluminescence (EL) test image if available

risks.risk: Output performance unverifiable (no load test shown)
risks.proof: Video or photo of multimeter/inverter showing live voltage and current under sunlight

risks.risk: Frame or junction box hidden damage not shown from all angles
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all four corners and the junction box seal

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the rear specification label showing brand, model, and wattage (Wp)
Video or photo of the panel under sunlight connected to a multimeter/inverter showing actual voltage/current output
Close-up photos of all four frame corners and the junction box, taken without glare
Photo of the front surface at an angle that avoids reflection, to check for cracks
response.reason: No brand, model, or wattage is legible on the panel in any photo, and wattage is the main determinant of a solar panel's price, so even a worst-case figure cannot be set until the rear label is readable.
